title: Black holes
summary: Schwarzschild spacetime as a vacuum with mass; curvature versus coordinate singularities via the Kretschmann scalar; radial infall in proper and coordinate time; the meaning of t and the horizon as a one-way surface; orbits of light and matter, the photon sphere and the innermost stable circular orbit.

objectives.description: Objectives will be finalised when the unit is prepared; the source material is 8.962 Lectures 21 (end), 22 and 23 (Lecture Guide pages 10–12), Tong Chapter 6 and Carroll Chapter 7.

preparation.description: Read the end of the Lecture Guide's Lecture 21 synopsis (PDF page 10): the Kretschmann scalar and radial infall in proper versus coordinate time.
Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of Lecture 22 (PDF page 11): the meaning of t, light propagation and the horizon.
Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of Lecture 23 (PDF page 12): testing black-hole spacetimes through the motion of light and matter.
Watch Lectures 22 and 23 (Black Holes I and II) from the video gallery (transcripts on each lecture page).
Second account: Tong, General Relativity, Chapter 6 Black Holes (reference-only).
Optional: Carroll, Chapter 7 The Schwarzschild Solution and Black Holes (second half), reference-only.
